hlni.insight: An appealing option and an available option are different questions.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume that because they like a subject, it is a core feature of the degree program they are considering.
hlni.viewerChange: Encourages students to move from passive preference to active verification of curriculum documents.

hlni.payoff: The student transitions from a vague preference to a concrete, actionable question.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA Preference Reality Check
objective: Teach students to distinguish between personal topic preferences and verified program availability.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: Student Writing Preference
shots.visual: A student sits at a desk with a notepad, writing 'Startup Law' under a 'Preference' header.
shots.dialogue: Trying to pick between B.Com and BBA? It is easy to confuse what you want with what is actually offered.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the notepad, steady hand.

shots.name: Method Reveal
shots.visual: The student draws a box next to 'Confirmed' and leaves it empty. They look at the camera.
shots.dialogue: Just because you love a topic doesn't mean the program includes it. Treat your preference as unverified until you check the official list.

shots.name: Practical Next Step
shots.visual: Student circles the empty box on their notepad, then looks up thoughtfully.
shots.dialogue: Ask yourself: Where is this module listed in the current curriculum? That is your next verification step.
shots.onscreenText: Where is this module listed in the current curriculum?
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the final question written on the notepad.

productionNotes.camera: Stable, hand-held feel, tight framing on the notepad.
productionNotes.editing: Simple cuts, focus on the writing action.
productionNotes.casting: A student looking at a potential degree choice.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Students often conflate their interests with program curriculum; the video teaches a verification method to check availability.

selected.title: The Preference Reality Check
selected.audienceGap: Students confuse their personal preference for a topic with the actual availability of that topic in a program.
selected.hlni: An appealing option and an available option are different questions. Unknown requirements should be recorded as checks rather than assumed to be satisfied.
selected.viewerChange: Helps students distinguish between what they like and what they have confirmed is available.
selected.concept: A student lists 'Entrepreneurship' as a preference but marks it as 'Unverified' in their checklist.
selected.device: A checklist overlay on the screen as the student speaks.
selected.support: The method distinguishes a desire from confirmation; it asserts no particular institutional rule.
methodSteps: List the actual requirements you need to check and mark unknowns.
Verify an unknown before treating the option as available.
selected.interpretationRule: Use an unknown requirement as the next verification task; preference alone is not confirmation.
selected.visibleProof: A preference card moves to a provisional list until one concrete requirement is checked.
selected.payoff: Use an unknown requirement as the next verification task; preference alone is not confirmation.
selected.limitations: Never invent eligibility rules, admission availability or prerequisites.

demonstration.observation: Realizing the 'preference' remains unchecked in the official course list.
